bestinet.meta: Research & Development · Cyberjaya, Selangor · Hybrid · Khazanah K-Youth placement
bestinet.b1: Took over a broken TOTP feature in an internal Flutter authenticator app where the one-time code never appeared on screen, and got it generating and displaying correctly.
bestinet.b2: Traced the failure with a numbered step-by-step trace through the generation chain and found two defects: the controller's init routine was never called from the view layer, and an invalid type cast on a secure-storage read threw on any device that was already enrolled.
bestinet.b3: Hardened the TOTP generation path by wrapping code generation in error handling and making a failed device or secret-key lookup return early instead of generating a code from an empty key.
bestinet.b4: Built the authenticator screen to the design I was given, with a countdown ring tied to the 30-second refresh window and the code rendered digit by digit, then applied the same supplied branding to the app shell and login screen.

projects.bestinet_desc: An internal Flutter authenticator app I worked on in Bestinet's R&D department. The TOTP feature was already written but never produced a code on screen, so my job was to find out why and make it work. I traced the generation chain step by step and found two faults: the controller's init routine was never triggered from the view layer, and a bad type cast on a secure-storage read threw on devices that were already enrolled, failing silently inside a swallowed error handler. I fixed both, then hardened the path so a failed secret lookup stops cleanly instead of generating from an empty key. Once codes were generating I built the screen to the design I was given, with a countdown ring tied to the 30-second window and the code laid out digit by digit, keeping the existing tap-to-copy. The code belongs to Bestinet, so there is no repository to link.
projects.silentsupport_desc: A private place to check in when feelings are heavy and words are hard. Tap one of eight feelings and a calm, pre-written response appears at once. A Supabase Edge Function asks a Llama model on Groq for a freshly written reply at the same depth, which takes its place only if it arrives within 2.5 seconds and passes a server-side tone filter that rejects questions, exclamation marks and stock phrases. History stays on the phone unless you sign in with an emailed code; sync merges both sides without dropping a check-in, row-level security scopes every row to its owner, and account deletion runs on the server. Built solo as an MVP with React Native (Expo), TypeScript and Supabase.
projects.baglock_desc: My final year project: a bag that opens to a fingerprint and calls for help when it does not. One enrolled finger toggles the servo, unlock on a touch and lock on the next, and with no screen the buzzer does all the talking, a different beep for boot, capture, match and refusal. Three failed matches in a row and it sounds the alarm, reads the GPS and texts a preset number twice, a plain warning then the coordinates to six decimal places. An Arduino Uno cannot listen on three software serial ports at once, so it opens each one in turn and brings the sensor back up afterwards.
projects.bookstore_desc: A PHP and MySQL bookstore with separate customer, seller and admin logins. Customers browse books, pay by card or cash, get a receipt and leave feedback. Sellers manage their listings and a pickup schedule for completed orders, which they can reschedule, and the admin side lists every purchase.
